mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in employment (PAYEMS) over 3 months predicts positive S&P 500 20-day returns due to stronger labor demand.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-month window, or 20-day returns not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during employment growth periods.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 exceeds its 3-month moving average by 2%, it triggers positive S&P 500 20-day returns as excess demand boosts equity valuations.
failure_condition: Returns not positive when GDPC1 crosses above MA by 2% in the subsequent 60 days, or no significant correlation (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in FEDFUNDS and rise in GDPC1 (demand) amplifies S&P 500 20-day returns through dual easing and demand expansion.
failure_condition: Returns not positively correlated with FEDFUNDS decline and GDPC1 rise over 5 days, or interaction effect rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market recovery regime (UNRATE < 3%), falling UNRATE triggers positive S&P 500 20-day returns as improved labor conditions boost consumer confidence.
failure_condition: UNRATE doesn't fall below 3% in the 3-month window preceding the return period, or returns not positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in INDPRO (supply) over 3 months signals robust production capacity, driving positive S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns not positive during sustained INDPRO growth periods, or no significant correlation (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% per annum, it triggers negative S&P 500 20-day returns due to higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: Returns not negative when FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the next 5 days, or no significant negative correlation (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in GDPC1 (demand) and PAYEMS (employment) strengthens S&P 500 20-day returns through expanded economic activity.
failure_condition: Returns not positively correlated with both GDPC1 and PAYEMS growth over 20 days, or interaction effect rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS increasing), persistent FEDFUNDS growth above 2% per annum predicts negative S&P 500 20-day returns due to higher interest rates.
failure_condition: Returns not negative during FEDFUNDS > 2% periods, or no significant negative correlation (t-test p > 0.05).
